design.text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled, multicenter trial; patients randomized 1:1:1 to imlunestrant, investigator's choice endocrine therapy (fulvestrant or exemestane), or an investigational combination regimen.

citations.quote: The efficacy of INLURYIO was evaluated in EMBER-3 (NCT04975308), a randomized, open-label, active-controlled, multicenter trial that enrolled 874 adult patients with ER+, HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, who were previously treated with an aromatase inhibitor either alone or in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

Patients were randomized 1:1:1 to INLURYIO 400 mg orally once daily; or investigator's choice of endocrine therapy (fulvestrant 500 mg IM on days 1, 15, 29, and once monthly thereafter (n=111) or exemestane 25 mg orally once daily (n=6)); or an additional investigational combination regimen.

population.text: Adults with ER+, HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with an aromatase inhibitor with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor; ESR1m population by ctDNA (N=256).

citations.quote: Among the patients on the INLURYIO arm or investigator's choice of endocrine therapy who were positive for ESR1m (N=256), the median age was 61 years (range: 28-85 years); all patients were female, of which 11% were pre/perimenopausal;

endpoint.text: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1 in the ESR1m population.

citations.quote: The major efficacy outcome was investigator assessed progression-free survival (PFS) according to RECIST v1.1.
The primary endpoints were investigator assessed progression free survival (PFS) in the *ESR1m* population and the ITT population (*ESR1m* and *ESR1m*-not detected).

indication.text: Treatment of adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.

citations.quote: INLURIYO is indicated for the treatment of adults with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, *estrogen receptor-1 (ESR1)*-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.

target_moa.text: Estrogen receptor antagonist that binds ER-alpha and induces its degradation, inhibiting ER-dependent gene transcription and proliferation in ER+ breast cancer cells.

citations.quote: Imlunestrant is an estrogen receptor (ER) antagonist that binds to ER\alpha. In vitro, imlunestrant induced degradation of ER\alpha, leading to inhibition of ER-dependent gene transcription and cellular proliferation in ER+ breast cancer cells.

modality.text: Small molecule (oral estrogen receptor antagonist / selective estrogen receptor degrader).

citations.quote: The recommended dosage of INLURIYO is 400 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

Imlunestrant is a next-generation orally bioavailable, noncovalent, SERD and antagonist. Imlunestrant binds with high affinity to wild-type and mutant (Y537S) ER\alpha and wild-type ER\beta ligand-binding domains with K_i values of 0.64 nM, 2.8 nM, and 0.11 nM, respectively.
NA = not applicable; OS = overall survival; PFS = progression-free survival; SERD = selective estrogen receptor degrader.

key_safety.text: Most common (>=10%) adverse reactions incl. lab abnormalities: hemoglobin decreased, musculoskeletal pain, calcium decreased, neutrophils decreased, AST increased, fatigue, diarrhea, ALT increased. Serious AEs in 10%; fatal AEs in 1.8%.

citations.quote: The most common (≥10%) adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, were hemoglobin decreased, musculoskeletal pain, calcium decreased, neutrophils decreased, AST increased, fatigue, diarrhea, ALT increased, triglycerides increased, nausea, platelets decreased, constipation, cholesterol increased, and abdominal pain.

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 10% of patients who received INLURYIO. Serious adverse reactions in > 1% of patients included pleural effusion (1.2%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.8% of patients who received INLURYIO, including cardiac arrest, acute myocardial infarction, right ventricular failure, hypovolemic shock, and upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage (each 0.3%).

detail.text: Guardant360 CDx assay, a ctDNA-based NGS test to detect specific ESR1 mutations, approved contemporaneously as a companion diagnostic.

citations.quote: CDRH considers this sPMA approvable as a companion diagnostic device to aid in detecting specific *ESR1* mutations in patients with breast cancer for treatment with INLURIYO (imlunestrant).

A supplemental Pre-Market Approval (PMA) Application (sPMA P200010/S021) was submitted to CDRH for the Guardant360 CDx assay. The sPMA will receive contemporaneous approval with this NDA as a companion diagnostic device for imlunestrant.
